title.narrative: Envelop 1: Supporting women and men by creating livelihood opportunities to respond to winterization and Cholera through on-the-job training and distributing small cash grants. And rehabilitation of roads to improve people's access to services and markets in the Ariha and Afrin districts.

description.narrative:
This project delivers an integrated set of interventions through responding to households who were affected by earthquake in NW Syria. And rehabilitation of the roads to improve people's access and movements in Idleb and Afrin areas. A) The first intervention aims to support 1,195 households affected by the earthquake through distributing multipurpose cash. This intervention aims to respond to earthquake-affected households of IDPs and HCs in Termanin, Sarmada, Besnaya - Bseineh, Atareb, Jandairis, Kafr Safra, Mhamadia, and Tal Slur by distributing multipurpose cash for one time. Where distribution of cash will support their steadfastness by providing basic needs of food and medicine, and other items. Every household will receive cash for one time with the value of 150 $ per one.
B) The second intervention aims to improve people's access to markets, livelihood opportunities, health, and other critical services by infrastructure restoration for affected communities to contribute to ER Efforts, and injections of cash through creating short-term livelihood opportunities. 1- Rehabilitation of two damaged roads, one between Kniseh and Ora Qabli with a length of 1300 meters. While the other is between Qatmet Efrin and kafar Janneh with a length of 1,100 meters through reparation of the body and the edges of the road. Those rehabilitation works will improve about 43,424 individuals’ access to services and markets in those four communities (Kniseh, Ora Qabli, Qatmet Efrin, kafar Janneh) and the surrounding villages. That rehabilitation works will improve access for 80 % of total pop. Where IHR NA proposed those projects. Each project includes Rehab works related to the market and road situation. 2- Creating short-term work opportunities by engaging 100 people (HCs and IDPs) in CFW to rehabilitate roads and markets.100 BNFs (20 females, 80 males, 10 % PWDs) will work for one month (26 days) against receiving 5 $ per workday
This project was designed and adapted to accommodate women and PWDs to be directly targeted to promote their access to employment and entrepreneurship opportunities. More details in activities
